slides.sub: Home blues parties. Stacks of vinyl. Bass you felt in the floor. Andre Williams grew up inside that frequency. Before he touched a drum machine, he already knew the weight of bass.

Before 'Original Nuttah', Andre apprenticed at Ariwa Studios under Mad Professor — the dub producer who fused reggae and technology into something alien. He learned to build space inside a track. That knowledge became jungle.
UK Apache. Iraqi father. Indian South African mother. Born and raised in London. Jamaican neighbors introduced him to soundsystem, dub, roots reggae. He took the culture in and made it his own.
UK Apache heard Shy FX's 'Gangsta Kid'. He walked in with lyrics written years before. 'Original Nuttah' was made. September 1994. SOUR Records. A 12-inch. 45 RPM. Underground. No promo budget.
Jamaica. India. Iraq. South London — fused into one frequency. This was ragga jungle: soundsystem bass meeting dancehall at breakneck speed over chopped breaks.

quote: People were trying to cheat me.
I had no one to trust.
slides.note: — UK Apache, on walking away at the peak
